newsitem.title: USA: Dole rained out in New Jersey battleground state.
newsitem.headline: Dole rained out in New Jersey battleground state.

text.p: Republican Bob Dole on Tuesday hoped his "Asphalt One" bus tour through New Jersey would help him win over this battleground state, but instead the tour was cut short by a tropical storm.

Dole held two brief campaign rallies, one damp, one soaked. He shook hands with patrons at a diner and coached a card game at a church social hall but then had to cancel two more outdoor rallies and a fundraiser to try to get home to Washington ahead of the remnants of Tropical Storm Josephine.

His speeches were standard stump material, stressing his promised 15 percent across-the-board tax cut, attacking President Bill Clinton's record on fighting illegal drugs, and pushing his weekend debate message that he was more trustworthy than the Democratic incumbent.
His most memorable line of the day came as a boisterous backer reached out to shake his hand after a rally and shouted, "Please get Bozo out of the White House."
"Bozo's on his way out," replied Dole, who has boasted of trying to stick to the issues and avoid namecalling, but who evidently could not ignore this opening.

Dole had planned an intensive two-day trip through New Jersey, a major investment of time in a swing state with 15 electoral votes that backed Clinton in 1992 and where opinion polls show Clinton has an edge of between 12 and 28 points.

Nationally, the latest tracking poll for Reuters by the Zogby Group International released on Tuesday found the race had narrowed considerably to a 5.3 percent margin. Clinton had 43.8 percent to Dole's 38.5 percent among 900 likely voters. Ross Perot had 4.5 percent, and 11.3 percent were undecided.

At the rally at the damp park in northern New Jersey, Dole stressed his themes of cutting taxes and fighting illegal drugs. He also pushed the message of his Sunday debate against Clinton, depicting himself as a man of his word in contrast with an unreliable Democrat who makes "empty promises."

"My word is good. I'll keep my promises to the American people," he told the rally in Lyndhurst. "I can give you example after example of Clinton saying one thing and then did another. When Bob Dole gives you his word you can go to the bank with it, he won't change his mind."

After a fairly upbeat first day of the bus tour on Monday, the morning after the debate where Dole was largely seen as doing better than many anticipated, Tuesday dawned gray and misty as tropical storm Josephine raced up the East Coast.

At the first rally, Dole stuck to an abbreviated version of his stump speech, speaking for only about 10 minutes. He reviewed his plan for an across-the-board 15 percent tax cut and explained how his tax policy would help families with young children, whom he calls "little tax credits."
"This is not a Wall Street tax cut," he said, as he had during Sunday's debate. "This is a family tax cut."
